title: iPhone Duo Screens Crack Along the Hinge Within Hours of $1,999 Foldable's Launch
excerpt: A handful of early owners report inner displays splitting at the fold — one after fewer than 20 openings. Apple has not commented, and the cause is unknown.
body:
• Several owners of Apple's first foldable, the $1,999 iPhone Duo, report the inner screen cracking along the hinge within hours of the October 23 launch.
  • The most detailed case: an Australian owner whose display split after about six hours and fewer than 20 openings, with no prior marks; an Apple Store replaced it on the spot.
  • Some photos appear to show demo units in China, and reviewers who folded test units hundreds of times report no such failure — the scale and cause are still unknown, and Apple has not commented.
  • If yours cracks: stop folding it, photograph the damage, and take it to Apple — hinge failure from normal use is covered by the one-year warranty, and launch-week buyers are inside the 14-day return window.

Apple's first foldable phone went on sale on Friday, October 23, and within hours a handful of owners were posting photographs of the same failure: the inner display cracked, or lit up with a bright line of dead pixels, right along the fold by the hinge, according to Gizmochina.

The most detailed account comes from an owner in Australia. He said he had owned the phone for about six hours and opened it fewer than 20 times. While showing it to a friend, he felt something under the screen near the internal hinge, heard a clear crack as he kept opening it, and the display split along the fold. There were no marks on the screen or the outside of the hinge suggesting anything had been caught or damaged. An Apple Store swapped the phone for a new one on the spot.

What is not yet known

Notebookcheck, summarising MacRumors and The Verge reporting, notes that other photographs on Reddit and the MacRumors forums show failures concentrated around the folding mechanism, some with bright horizontal lines across part of the inner screen. But the circumstances of several photographs — including images reportedly taken of demonstration units in China, which are handled constantly — remain unclear.

https://x.com/MacRumors/status/2113693360729002145

Early reviewers who deliberately folded their units hundreds of times have not reported the same issue, though that sample is small. It is too early to say whether the reports point to a design flaw, a bad production batch, or isolated mishaps. Apple had made no public statement as of Saturday, and the number of affected devices is unknown. The company is likely collecting returned units for analysis.

Why the stakes are high for Apple

The Duo is Apple's first entry into foldables, a category Samsung and others have sold for years, and it is priced accordingly: $1,999 in the United States, with a 7.6-inch folding OLED inner display and a 5.4-inch outer screen. Apple has emphasised the durability of its precision-engineered hinge and multilayer inner display. A hinge-line crack on day one — even in a handful of units — strikes at exactly the claim the product is sold on, which is why the company's response, and whether failures cluster in particular batches, will matter more than the initial posts.

If you bought one

So far this is a small number of reported cases in a large global launch. Owners whose phones fold normally can keep using them, but should treat a sudden change in hinge feel, a crunching sensation, or a bright line along the crease as warning signs. The guidance collected by TechCheatCodes is the sensible course: stop folding the device, document the damage, and take it to Apple rather than attempting any fix. Hinge failures from normal use fall under the standard one-year warranty, and anyone who bought this week is also inside the 14-day return window.
